 9               THE SECRETARY:   Extraordinary 

10  Session Legislative Resolution Number 2, 

11  commemorating Wednesday, December 7, 20ll, as 

12  Pearl Harbor Remembrance Day in the State of 

13  New York.

14               "WHEREAS, It is the sense of this 

15  Legislative Body to commemorate significant events 

16  which represent turning points in our unique 

17  history and which are indelibly etched in the saga 

18  of our great nation; and 

19               "WHEREAS, Attendant to such concern, 

20  and in full accord with its long-standing 

21  traditions, this Legislative Body is justly proud 

22  to commemorate Wednesday, December 7, 2011, as 

23  Pearl Harbor Remembrance Day in the State of 

24  New York; and 

25               "WHEREAS, On December 7, 1941, the 

                                                                6354

 1  Imperial Japanese Navy launched a surprise attack 

 2  on the United States naval base at Pearl Harbor on 

 3  Oahu, Hawaii, destroying 188 aircraft, five 

 4  battleships, one minelayer and three destroyers, 

 5  with more than 2,400 dead and 1,100 wounded; and 

 6               "WHEREAS, A decisive victory for the 

 7  Japanese, the attack on Pearl Harbor spurred the 

 8  United States into a declaration of war.  The 

 9  country officially entered World War II the 

10  following day, when President Franklin Delano 

11  Roosevelt addressed a joint session of Congress, 

12  calling December 7, 1941, 'a date that will live 

13  in infamy'; and 

14               "WHEREAS, Four days after the attack 

15  on Pearl Harbor, Japan's allies, Nazi Germany and 

16  Fascist Italy, declared war on the United States, 

17  turning it into a global war and opening up the 

18  Atlantic theater; and 

19               "WHEREAS, Despite the perception of 

20  the attack on Pearl Harbor as a devastating blow 

21  to America, the three aircraft carriers assigned 

22  to the Pacific Fleet -- the Enterprise, the 

23  Lexington, and the Saratoga -- remained intact, as 

24  did the navy yard and submarine base, and tank 

25  farms were undamaged; and 

                                                                6355

 1               "WHEREAS, However, the battleships 

 2  Arizona and Oklahoma and the destroyers Shaw, 

 3  Cassin and Downes, were permanently lost, and 

 4  several other battleships were removed from the 

 5  order of battle to be refitted; and 

 6               "WHEREAS, The attack on Pearl Harbor 

 7  immediately galvanized a divided nation into 

 8  action.  At the time, public opinion had been 

 9  moving towards support for entering the war but 

10  considerable opposition still remained; and 

11               "WHEREAS, Overnight, Americans 

12  united against their enemies, and the 'sleeping 

13  giant' of United States industrial and military 

14  capacity was awakened, pouring overwhelming 

15  resources into both the Pacific and Atlantic 

16  theaters toward final victory over tyranny; and 

17               "WHEREAS, Over 16 million Americans 

18  ultimately served in the armed forces during 

19  World War II, with over 400,000 paying the 

20  ultimate sacrifice for their country; and 

21               "WHEREAS, Countless veterans and 

22  active-duty soldiers have been inspired by the 

23  spirit of courage, duty and sacrifice displayed by 

24  those men and women who served at Pearl Harbor on 

25  December 7, 1941; and 

                                                                6356

 1               "WHEREAS, It is the custom of this 

 2  Legislative Body that when events of such 

 3  historical consequences are brought to our 

 4  attention, they should be celebrated and 

 5  recognized by all citizens of this great Empire 

 6  State; now, therefore, be it 

 7               "RESOLVED, That this Legislative 

 8  Body pause in its deliberations to commemorate 

 9  Wednesday, December 7, 2011, as Pearl Harbor 

10  Remembrance Day in the State of New York."

11               ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Senator 

12  Larkin.

13               SENATOR LARKIN:   Thank you, 

14  Mr. President.

15               You know, there's very few of us 

16  here today that were alive on that day 70 years 

17  ago.  It was a Sunday morning.  Most of the 

18  troops, both Navy, Army, coastal units, were 

19  having breakfast.  And the sound of it was 

20  something that was a shriek, if you've ever been 

21  there when they show the movie at Pearl Harbor.  

22  The number of 600 are still floating down there in 

23  the USS Arizona.  

24               Pearl Harbor did something.  It woke 

25  us up.  I remember that Sunday I went to the 

                                                                6357

 1  movies in McDonald's area, the Troy Theater, and 

 2  we come out and they said "Pearl Harbor's been 

 3  bombed," because it was different hours here.  

 4  People had no idea where Pearl Harbor was:  

 5  "What's the Navy doing out there?  What are the 

 6  Army folks doing out there?"

 7               Twenty-four hundred were killed and 

 8  1100 were wounded.  We lost the intensity that we 

 9  should have had to engage the Japanese strongly 

10  enough.  We had military leaders that weren't 

11  listening to Washington, and they moved the fleet 

12  out into the ocean.  The Army took care of 

13  themselves because of their ack-acks, and 

14  everybody else was handling a gun, even nurses.

15               This is a day that we never should 

16  miss.  Today in Hawaii they had the last ceremony 

17  they will have because there are just so few of 

18  them alive today.  But what is it all about?  It's 

19  about our country.  

20               Hawaii wasn't a state, Hawaii was a 

21  territory of the United States of America.  To be 

22  assigned to Hawaii in those days was considered 

23  the golden spot for any member of the armed 

24  forces.  Today it is still one of the bright spots 

25  in our military commands.  But when you go to 

                                                                6358

 1  Hawaii, nobody lets you forget what went on.  

 2  First thing they want to do is to take you to the 

 3  Arizona.  Then they want to take you to 

 4  Hickam Field, and you see what happened, where it 

 5  was, and why we did what we did.  

 6               The bravery of the men and women at 

 7  Pearl Harbor and at Hickam, you have to see the 

 8  story of it to see what those men and women went 

 9  through, and the families.  I've met children who 

10  are now my age whose family was there, they were 

11  stationed there, and they told of the bravery.  

12  They said if somebody got wounded, people just 

13  didn't walk away, they turned around:  What can we 

14  do to help?  

15               I think it woke America up.  Because 

16  we had a lot of people in this country at that 

17  time who said why are we getting involved in this 

18  business.  Well, for two years before the Japanese 

19  attacked us, we sent all of our salvage material, 

20  metal, to Japan.  And two years later they come 

21  back with bombers and bombed us.

22               Pearl Harbor should never be 

23  forgotten.  Old-timers like Dean Skelos said to 

24  me:  "Remember the Alamo."  I said "I wasn't that 

25  old, Dean." 

                                                                6359

 1               (Laughter.)

 2               SENATOR LARKIN:   But we should 

 3  never forget Pearl Harbor.  Units that were at 

 4  Pearl Harbor then -- the 25th Infantry Division, 

 5  the Pineapple, the 24th -- later engaged in the 

 6  South Pacific, but their heart and soul was at 

 7  Pearl Harbor.  

 8               I wasn't old enough to be there.  

 9  I've been there twice during my military career.  

10  And I want to tell you, the people that were alive 

11  then say if it was not for the American forces and 

12  the stability, the foresight for both Short and 

13  Kincaid, the Navy and Army officers who later 

14  everybody wanted to crucify because somebody in 

15  Washington dropped the ball, well, the easiest 

16  thing to do was to hang the general and the 

17  admiral.  If the general and the admiral had not 

18  acted, there would have been more than 2400 

19  killed.  

20               So today is a day we should never 

21  forget.  President Roosevelt said it the day 

22  after, when he said "the day of infamy."  But you 

23  know what, if you think this country is doing 

24  something right, remember, it took the heart and 

25  soul of members of the armed forces to stand up.  

                                                                6360

 1  Nobody ran away.  Oh, yes, somebody said the fleet 

 2  went out, the fleet went out and attacked the 

 3  Japanese.  And 2400 people were killed, 1100 were 

 4  wounded.  It was reported that in 60 days, over 

 5  200 of those wounded died of wounds.

 6               So, you know, it's nice and easy to 

 7  sit here today and say "I don't remember Pearl 

 8  Harbor."  Some of you don't even remember 

 9  Vietnam.  And I think our nation has to make sure 

10  that our generations of the future understand what 

11  our country's all about, the greatest country in 

12  the world.  

13               And I say, in prayer, God bless 

14  those who helped us survive as a nation.  

15               Thank you very much.

 5               SENATOR DeFRANCISCO:   Thank you, 

 6  Mr. President.

 7               I'll be brief because the hour is 

 8  late.  However, this package is an excellent 

 9  example of how we can work in a bipartisan fashion 

10  in order to compromise and do what's good for the 

11  citizens of the State of New York, rather than 

12  take intractable positions and be unwilling to get 

13  a result.  And I think that's what we've seen 

14  repeatedly over this last year.

15               The centerpiece of this whole piece 

16  of legislation is really the change in the tax 

17  brackets in the State of New York.  And by this 

18  change, 205,299 taxpayers will have a surcharge 

19  eliminated that they've had to pay over these last 

20  two years.  Four million four hundred forty-two- 

21  thousand-plus individuals will actually receive 

22  tax cuts under this package.  

23               There's a payroll reduction, there's 

24  a reduction in the MTA payroll tax.  A tax cut for
